U.S. Bitcoin ETFs Lose $261 Million, Ether ETFs Shed $130 Million According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $261 million in net outflows on October 14, with Bitwise's BITB posting the largest inflow at $2.22 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $130 million in net outflows, led by BlackRock's ETHA with $110 million. — link

Binance ETH Long Liquidations Top $106 Million in One Hour, Highest in Six Months According to CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost, hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation triggered more than $106 million in ETH long liquidations on Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange by trading volume, within one hour — the largest hourly liquidation of ETH longs on the platform in nearly six months. Darkfost noted that crypto futures trading volume is now roughly nine times spot volume, making highly leveraged markets more vulnerable to macroeconomic shocks. He added that expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike have risen from 17% to nearly 30% in one week, intensifying pressure on derivatives markets. — link

Just In: Former Binance Futures Head's Perp DEX StandX to Shut Down, Scrap Token Launch StandX, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange founded by former Binance Futures head Aaron Gong and other industry veterans, announced it will shut down operations and abandon plans to launch a platform token following a business and market review. Since its November 2025 mainnet launch, StandX says it has served over 237,000 users and reached peak TVL of more than $200 million. Yield distributions will end on October 15, while perpetual trading will become reduce-only on October 20. All remaining positions will be closed by January 15, 2027, with DUSD redemptions and asset withdrawals closing January 31. The team plans a one-time DUSD airdrop funded by remaining revenue and additional team contributions. — link

Hyperliquid Founder Jeff Yan Says US Regulation Should Target Market Operators, Not the Underlying Blockchain Hyperliquid founder Jeff Yan told Bloomberg's Odd Lots podcast that US regulators should treat Hyperliquid's Layer 1 blockchain as financial infrastructure rather than a traditional exchange, with regulatory obligations falling on firms that deploy and operate markets on the network. Yan argued that oversight should apply to entities exercising control over those markets, allowing the protocol to function as a shared liquidity and trading infrastructure layer. Bloomberg noted that Kraken parent Payward plans to offer derivatives to US investors using Hyperliquid technology through a regulated exchange. Yan said Hyperliquid aims to provide infrastructure for Wall Street institutions rather than replace them. Hyperliquid remains unavailable to US users. — link
